'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.
== External Links == * [https://www.natsuzora.com/may/park/takashimayama.html Takashimayama Park]

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.

His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[November 22]], [[1832]] – [[October 16]], [[1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[entrepreneur]] and [[divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[1859]] ([[Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)|12=draft|12=draft}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.
