Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[Taishō]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
== Related Articles == *{{ill|Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|JA|高島駅 (北海道)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takashima Station (Hokkaido)|qq=}} – A station named after the agricultural land he managed in Hokkaido. *[[Honmachi Elementary School (Yokohama)]] – Built on the site of Yokohama Gas Company, preserving a gas lamp as a monument.
== External Links == * [https://www.natsuzora.com/may/park/takashimayama.html Takashimayama Park]

He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

; Awards * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.
== Honors == ; Rank * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]] * [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]
; Awards * [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. '''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, [[:en:November 22|November 22]], [[:en:1832|1832]] – [[:en:October 16|October 16]], [[:en:1914|1914]]) was a [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]-based [[:en:Entrepreneur|Entrepreneur]] and [[:en:Divination|I Ching scholar]] active during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]]'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern [[:en:Chūō, Tokyo|Chūō ward]], [[:en:Ginza|Ginza]]), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the [[:en:Four Books and Five Classics|Four Books and Five Classics]]. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In [[:en:1859|1859]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the [[:en:I Ching|I Ching]].

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of [[:en:Harry Parkes|Harry Parkes]], the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 18|July 18]] – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* [[:en:1914|1914]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō era]] 3), [[:en:October 16|October 16]] – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* [[:en:1887|1887]] ([[Meiji]] 20), [[:en:July 20|July 20]] – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* [[:en:1902|1902]] ([[Meiji]] 35), [[:en:February 22|February 22]] – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at [[:en:Sengaku-ji|Sengaku-ji]], and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
