'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching}}.

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 18|en|July 18|WD=Q2730|lt=July 18}} – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914}} ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|WD=Q329174|lt=Taishō era}} 3), {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16}} – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 20|en|July 20|WD=Q2728|lt=July 20}} – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* {{ill|1902|en|1902|WD=Q2043|lt=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|WD=Q2351|lt=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching}}.
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

; Awards * {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 20|en|July 20|WD=Q2728|lt=July 20}} – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * {{ill|1902|en|1902|WD=Q2043|lt=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|WD=Q2351|lt=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching}}.

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 18|en|July 18|WD=Q2730|lt=July 18}} – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914}} ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|WD=Q329174|lt=Taishō era}} 3), {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16}} – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 20|en|July 20|WD=Q2728|lt=July 20}} – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* {{ill|1902|en|1902|WD=Q2043|lt=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|WD=Q2351|lt=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. {{unreferenced|date=June 2012}} {{Special characters|description=[[Microsoft Code Page 932]] ([[hashigo-daka]])}} {{Infobox person | name = Kaemon Takashima | furigana = たかしま かえもん | image = File:Kaemon Takashima.png | image_size = 200px | caption = Portrait in his later years | birth_date = 1832; {{birth date|1832|12|24}} | birth_place = {{ill|Edo|WD=Q215646|1=Edo}} | death_date = 1914; {{death date|1914|10|16}} | renamed = Seisaburō (childhood name), Kahē, Kaemon | death_place = | cause_of_death = | resting_place = {{ill|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|1=Sengaku-ji}} | nationality = {{ill|Japan|WD=Q17|1=Japan}} | alma_mater = | occupation = {{ill|businessperson|WD=Q43845|1=Businessperson}}; {{ill|oracle|WD=Q217123|1=Oracle}} | notable_works = "Takashima Eidan" | influenced = | influences = | awards = {{ill|Order of the Sacred Treasure, 4th class|WD=Q56561438|1=Order of the Sacred Treasure, 4th class}} | gender = {{ill|male|WD=Q6581097|1=Male (gender)}} | native_name = 高島 嘉右衛門 | given_name = {{ill|Kaemon|WD=Q116980329|1=Kaemon}} }}
'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

; Awards * {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887|1=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 20|en|July 20|WD=Q2728|lt=July 20|1=July 20}} – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * {{ill|1902|en|1902|WD=Q2043|lt=1902|1=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|WD=Q2351|lt=February 22|1=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji|1=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

{{unreferenced|date=June 2012}} {{Special characters|description=[[Microsoft Code Page 932]] ([[hashigo-daka]])}} {{Infobox person | name = Kaemon Takashima | furigana = たかしま かえもん | image = File:Kaemon Takashima.png | image_size = 200px | caption = Portrait in his later years | birth_date = 1832; {{birth date|1832|12|24}} | birth_place = {{ill|Edo|WD=Q215646|1=Edo}} | death_date = 1914; {{death date|1914|10|16}} | renamed = Seisaburō (childhood name), Kahē, Kaemon | death_place = | cause_of_death = | resting_place = {{ill|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|1=Sengaku-ji}} | nationality = {{ill|Japan|WD=Q17|1=Japan}} | alma_mater = | occupation = {{ill|businessperson|WD=Q43845|1=Businessperson}}; {{ill|oracle|WD=Q217123|1=Oracle}} | notable_works = "Takashima Eidan" | influenced = | influences = | awards = {{ill|Order of the Sacred Treasure, 4th class|WD=Q56561438|1=Order of the Sacred Treasure, 4th class}} | gender = {{ill|male|WD=Q6581097|1=Male (gender)}} | native_name = 高島 嘉右衛門 | given_name = {{ill|Kaemon|WD=Q116980329|1=Kaemon}} }}
'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

; Awards * {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887|1=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 20|en|July 20|WD=Q2728|lt=July 20|1=July 20}} – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]] * {{ill|1902|en|1902|WD=Q2043|lt=1902|1=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|WD=Q2351|lt=February 22|1=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]
== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji|1=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."
== Entrepreneur == Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.
=== Imprisonment === In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development === Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.
In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.
== I Ching Scholar == === Takashima Eidan === Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Legacy == Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji|1=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

* {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}} ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|WD=Q329174|lt=Taishō era|1=Taishō era}} 3), {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}} – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

* {{ill|1902|en|1902|WD=Q2043|lt=1902|1=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|WD=Q2351|lt=February 22|1=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji|1=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. '''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

; Rank

* {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}} ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|WD=Q329174|lt=Taishō era|1=Taishō era}} 3), {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}} – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* {{ill|1887|en|1887|WD=Q7826|lt=1887|1=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 20|en|July 20|WD=Q2728|lt=July 20|1=July 20}} – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* {{ill|1902|en|1902|WD=Q2043|lt=1902|1=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|WD=Q2351|lt=February 22|1=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji|1=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|WD=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|WD=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|WD=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|WD=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|WD=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|WD=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|WD=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|WD=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|WD=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|WD=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In {{ill|1859|en|1859|WD=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|WD=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|WD=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji|1=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."

'''Kaemon Takashima''' (たかしま かえもん, {{ill|November 22|en|November 22|qid=Q3025|lt=November 22|1=November 22}}, {{ill|1832|en|1832|qid=Q7584|lt=1832|1=1832}} – {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|qid=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}}, {{ill|1914|en|1914|qid=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}}) was a {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|qid=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}-based {{ill|Entrepreneur|en|Entrepreneur|qid=Q131524|lt=Entrepreneur|1=Entrepreneur}} and {{ill|Divination|en|Divination|qid=Q1043197|lt=I Ching scholar|1=Divination}} active during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|qid=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu|1=Bakumatsu}} and [[Meiji]] periods. Born in Edo's Sanjikkenbori district, his childhood name was Seisaburō, later renamed Kahē and finally Kaemon. He also used the pen name Donshō (呑象). His achievements in {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|qid=Q38283|lt=Yokohama|1=Yokohama}}'s development earned him recognition as one of the "Three Great Men of Yokohama," alongside [[Kanbee Yoshida]] and [[Seihei Karube]]. His legacy lives on in places such as [[Takashimacho, Yokohama]]. He is also known for authoring "Takashima Eidan."

== Entrepreneur ==
Born the sixth child in Edo's [[Sanjikkenbori River|Sanjikkenbori district]] (modern {{ill|Chūō, Tokyo|en|Chūō, Tokyo|qid=Q212704|lt=Chūō ward|1=Chūō, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Ginza|en|Ginza|qid=Q746052|lt=Ginza|1=Ginza}}), Takashima was the son of Yakuji Kahē from the "Enshūya" lumber business. His early years were marked by exceptional memory and intellect, excelling in the {{ill|Four Books and Five Classics|en|Four Books and Five Classics|qid=Q1377760|lt=Four Books and Five Classics|1=Four Books and Five Classics}}. He inherited his father’s lumber business at a young age, later expanding into other industries.

=== Imprisonment ===
In {{ill|1859|en|1859|qid=Q7687|lt=1859|1=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|qid=Q1327259|lt=Ansei|1=Ansei}} 6), Takashima opened a trading house in Yokohama dealing in [[:en:Imari porcelain|Imari porcelain]] and other goods. However, he was arrested for illicitly selling [[kobans]] to foreigners, violating currency exchange laws, and served a prison term. It was during this imprisonment that he immersed himself in the study of the {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|qid=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.

=== Contribution to Yokohama's Development ===
Takashima played a critical role in Yokohama's urban expansion. Notably, he initiated land reclamation projects that transformed the city's infrastructure. He collaborated with [[Richard Bridgens]], an American engineer, and earned the trust of {{ill|Harry Parkes|en|Harry Parkes|qid=Q5671468|lt=Harry Parkes|1=Harry Parkes}}, the British Minister to Japan, leading to numerous construction projects.

In {{ill|1872|en|1872|qid=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), Takashima founded Japan's first gas company, [[Yokohama Gas Company]], and successfully lit Yokohama's streets with gas lamps. His efforts in urban planning and infrastructure development established him as a pioneer in modernizing Yokohama.

== I Ching Scholar ==
=== Takashima Eidan ===
Takashima's divination abilities became legendary, earning him the title of "Eisei" (易聖, "Saint of Divination"). His predictions, such as foreseeing the [[Ansei Earthquake]] and major political events, gained him widespread fame. After his retirement, Takashima devoted himself to studying and teaching the I Ching, culminating in the publication of "Takashima Eidan." The work was well-received internationally and translated into Chinese and English.

== Honors ==
; Rank
* {{ill|1887|en|1887|qid=Q7826|lt=1887|1=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 18|en|July 18|qid=Q2730|lt=July 18|1=July 18}} – [[Junior Fifth Rank]]
* {{ill|1914|en|1914|qid=Q2083|lt=1914|1=1914}} ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō era|1=Taishō era}} 3), {{ill|October 16|en|October 16|qid=Q2963|lt=October 16|1=October 16}} – [[Senior Fifth Rank]]

; Awards
* {{ill|1887|en|1887|qid=Q7826|lt=1887|1=1887}} ([[Meiji]] 20), {{ill|July 20|en|July 20|qid=Q2728|lt=July 20|1=July 20}} – [[Order of the Sacred Treasure, Fourth Class]]
* {{ill|1902|en|1902|qid=Q2043|lt=1902|1=1902}} ([[Meiji]] 35), {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|qid=Q2351|lt=February 22|1=February 22}} – [[Gold Rays with Rosette]]

== Legacy ==
Takashima’s influence extended beyond his lifetime, with his name still associated with various institutions and geographical locations. His remains were interred at {{ill|Sengaku-ji|en|Sengaku-ji|qid=Q3176144|lt=Sengaku-ji|1=Sengaku-ji}}, and his posthumous Buddhist name was "Taikan'in Jinei Donshō Koji."
